# Review, pass 1 — hammurabi-laws-100-111

Reviewer pass 1 (adversarial), run on the routine's model. Inputs: RUNBOOK §2, conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, linecheck.md, units.json, the published parts (checked in detail against `hammurabi-laws-26-41`, `-52-65`, `-gap-b`), Harper's autograph plates (PDF pp. 267, 269, 271, 273), Harper's List of Signs and List of Numerals, and Harper's glossary (text layer, PDF pp. 182–209) as a lexical aid. No modern translation was opened. `units.json` was edited in place by script (`scratchpad/scripts/review1_apply.py`; the untouched draft is saved as `scratchpad/units.pass1.orig.json`). No sign was added (GI4 was already in the glossary); `signs.py check` prints "in sync". Nothing was built or validated (no build this pass).

Counts: 1 high, 5 medium, 9 low (15 changes); 12 findings or checks refused or left, listed below.

## What was checked, and how far

- **Plates.** All four plates were aligned row by row against Harper's margin numerals and against the line content (the plate has line 35 running over the page-turn: its last three signs, bi-ša-am, are the first row of Plate XXVII; every later row follows from that). Every row that holds a logogram or a sign the caller named was viewed at 6–14× and compared with Harper's List of Signs (entries 12, 19, 26, 42, 50, 79, 83, 89, 94, 97, 99, 101, 116, 121, 122, 133, 142, 161, 177, 178, 181, 190, 204) and with the List of Numerals. Rows seen at high zoom: XVII 1–6, 13, 15–35 (in 3–5 row strips), 36–47, 52–56, 57–66, 66–67, 69; XVIII 12–13, 16–21, 25–28, 32–33, 36–37, 39–41, 46–49. For the remaining rows the sign count and the gross shapes of the recurring signs (A, NA, I, DI, IN, AD, SA, TAG, MA, the fused ŠÀ.GAN₂ group, LÁ, KÙ.BABBAR, BI/GEŠ/KAŠ, AN) were matched. Phonetic signs were **not** each identified by shape: the counts and shapes agree with the draft everywhere seen, and the draft's line division (word counts per Harper line, 121 lines, only the five numeral/Sumerogram lines differ in word count) agrees with Harper's. A second pass should still read XVII 7–12, 14, 29–31, 38–45, 48–51, 58–60, 68, 70–72 and XVIII 1–11, 14–15, 22–24, 29–31, 34–35, 38, 42–45 sign by sign if time allows.
- **Confirmed on the plate:** UD-mi-šu (XVII 4); SIG (XVII 34: ŠE, SIG, Ì, GIŠ, four signs); a-du III-šu with DU, not DI (XVII 66); 6 (XVIII 12); ŠÁM (XVIII 16; long KA wedge with three signs inside, as Harper's no. 83); KAŠ = the same sign as GEŠ/BI (no. 94: XVIII 16, 20, 40, 46) and in GEŠ.TIN.NA = nos. 94, 178, 30 (XVIII 26, 39, 41); KI.LAM (XVIII 20–21, as no. 177 "mahîru"); NA₄ (XVIII 18, two pieces, as no. 97); É (concentric corners, as no. 121: XVIII 28, 39, 41) and É.GAL (XVIII 32: A, NA, É, GAL); MAL.GE.A (XVIII 37; MAL = no. 101, GE = no. 122, A = no. 204); the 60 (single tall wedge) and U.SA.KA.NI (XVIII 46: 60, KAŠ, U, SA, KA, NI); BURU₁₄ (XVIII 48: two pieces, as no. 19); line 49 = fused "50 KA" sign (Harper's numeral list), ŠE, i, li, qi (five signs).
- **Not resolved on the plate:** the split of the fused first two signs of ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ (see the refused list); the identity of SAL and NIN (Harper's List of Signs nos. 192–202 are missing from the scan: PDF p. 410 is blank), so ŠAL and NIN were checked by position and count only (XVIII 36: šum, ma, ŠAL, NIN (a two-piece group), AN, five signs).

## Checked and left (no change), and findings refused

1. **`reading` from glyph `tr`.** Rebuilt by script for every word: all match (the two "a-du 3-šu" / "a-du 6-šu" are the published form). No ḳ anywhere (the draft already writes q, `IG` = ik/iq as Harper prints, as the published parts do).
2. **ln/p, first unit.** Unit 0 (XVII 1–7, tail of §100) has no ln/p and stays so; ln/p stand on the first unit of §101–111 only; unit boundaries and law starts match Harper's headings (XVII 8, 15, 24, 32, 46, 55, 68; XVIII 15, 26, 36, 45).
3. **Numerals as role `log`:** kept; it is what `-52-65` (20, 60, 4, ½), `-11-25` (5, 6) and `-gap-b` (1, 6) do, and the conventions' own `num` role has not been used by any published part. 5BAN₂ and the single 60 follow the same pattern.
4. **ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ split kept** (not refused outright, but not fixed): see change 7; one cannot tell from the fused plate shape whether Harper's "SA.GAN" or the modern ŠÀ + GAN₂ is the better split. Left as the working convention; for QUESTIONS.md.
5. **BI for KAŠ/GEŠ kept:** Harper's no. 94 lists GEŠ, bi, kaz, šikaru as one sign and the plate shows one shape in all of them.
6. **SIG kept:** matched to Harper's glossary (šipâtu) and, loosely, to his no. 190 (šipâtu); the plate sign (a box with a long wedge) is not a certain shape match; the note already says so.
7. **ŠÁM glyph kept:** the plate sign is the long KA wedge with three signs inside, as Harper's no. 83; the Unicode form KA × (GAR + ŠÀ + A) is by shape; the inner signs on the plate were not individually identified.
8. **"disowned his merchant" (§106) kept.** nakārum with a person as object is "to disown, deny"; "denied his merchant" is stilted English and `l` keeps "he-denied". The about uses the same word for §106 and §107, so the two laws read alike.
9. **"criminals" for ṣarrūtum kept.** Generic English; Harper's "outlaws, rowdies, traitors" is quoted in the note. No phrase-level overlap with any version I could recognise was found in `i`; I looked at §103, §104, §105, §107 and §108–110 in particular. Closest: "a sealed receipt … silver without a sealed receipt shall not be entered in the account" (§105): the Akkadian dictates the clause, and "sealed receipt" is Harper's own glossary term; kept. "swear the oath of the god", "by the heavy weight" are our own renderings.
10. **i-sa-ad-dar-ma (XVII 3, 39) kept as sadārum.** The plate shows SA (nested corners), not ŠA. The published `-26-41` has i-ša-ad-dar under šaṭārum; Harper lists both under one entry. Flagged for QUESTIONS.md; the note already says Harper has it under šaṭāru.
11. **nikkazzim, bīt karānim kept** on Harper's readings, with the later readings named in the notes (nikkassum; the tavern).
12. **"the stele writes ga-ga-ad", "tadmiqtum 'kindness'", "pašārum 'trade'":** checked against Harper's glossary (GAGGADU, TADMIKTU "favor", PASARU "to trade", DIPTU "credit(?)", NIKKAZZU "account, credit", KANIKU, SARRUTU, MAḪARU, KAPU "to intrust"): all as the draft says.

## Remembered English, grammar labels, l ↔ i

Every grammatical label in every note was checked against the form (the only wrong ones were changes 3 and 5). `l` was checked word by word against the original for all 21 units; no mismatch. `l` ↔ `i`: all agree in sense and force; where `i` supplies what the grammar leaves out (§107 "denied having received", §100 the subject) the note says so. Sumerogram `val`/`say`: stems in `val`, case in `say`, checked for every Sumerogram (one case error, change 4).

## For the second pass, the glosser and conventions

- Glosser: **ugbabtum** — entry must read "priestess (NIN.AN = NIN.DINGIR; later editions read ugbabtum; UNCERTAIN)"; not nadītum. **wašārum** — broaden: ūtaššar is the Dt present, "he shall be released". **leqûm** — ilqēma is a preterite. **nakārum** — the gap-b entry is built on one broken form and says UNCERTAIN; the stele gives ittakir (perfect), ikkiru (preterite + -u), "to deny, dispute" (Harper "to dispute"). **šamallûm** — the gap-b entry says the syllabic spellings are a placeholder; the stele writes the logogram ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ. **pašārum, šanûm-Š, qaqqadum, ṣibtum** — gap-b entries are marked uncertain; the stele now supplies the spelled forms (Harper "to trade"; "to duplicate, to double"). New lemmas: manûm-count, redûm-lead (homograph-safe names are in the draft), qiāpum, egûm, sadārum, rakāsum-N, nadûm-Š, tadmiqtum, kanīkum, nikkazzum, dibtum, ṣarrūtum, sābītum, gagûm, usakani (untranslated), 3-šu, 6-šu, 5 BAN₂. A second pass should check each against the text.
- conventions.md (house renderings to add): šamallûm "agent"; ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA (sābītum) "tavern-keeper"; kanīkum "sealed receipt"; ina abnim rabîtim "by the heavy weight"; tamkāršu ittakir "disowned his merchant"; nīš ilim izakkar "swear the oath of the god"; nikkazzum "the account"; ūtaššar is a Dt form; spelling note: ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ and SAL.NIN.AN (read ugbabtum, uncertain), MAL.GE.A (GÁ.GI₄.A, GI4 with tr GE).
- QUESTIONS.md: (a) Harper's List of Signs nos. 192–202 are not in the Cornell scan (PDF p. 410 blank), so SAL, NIN and neighbours cannot be compared with the list; the Toronto copy (page + 4) is not in the repository. (b) First two signs of ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ are one fused group on the plate; the ŠÀ + GAN₂ split is a convention. (c) §110 NIN.AN read ugbabtum (uncertain; Harper gives none; the draft's nadītum was withdrawn); §127 and §178–179 (later parts) must read it the same way. (d) i-sa-ad-dar: sadārum here vs šaṭārum in `-26-41`. (e) The 60 in §111 is one tall wedge with no measure sign; "sixty qa" is Harper's expansion. (f) The plate's line 35 runs across the Plate XXVI/XXVII page turn (bi-ša-am is the first row of XXVII).
